findings.title: Double-clicking a name to copy it still toggles the row once
findings.body: The guard covers a drag-select, but not a double- or triple-click, which is the other common way to select a name. In Chromium the first click's `click` fires while nothing is selected yet, so line 217 toggles the row. The word only gets selected on the second mousedown, so only the second `click` is skipped. The net result is one toggle plus a selection, which is the same side effect the earlier thread described. Two possible fixes: on the row's `onMouseDown`, call `preventDefault()` when `event.detail > 1` (but that blocks word selection), or compare `event.detail` and undo the first toggle when `detail === 2`. If double-click copying isn't a goal, a comment saying so would be enough.

contracts.action: A click on a selectable finding row is ignored when the window has a non-empty text selection
contracts.equivalent_path: The checkbox's own onChange (Check → setFixing) at reconcile-dialog.tsx:230; the row click skips input targets at line 214 so the box toggles once
contracts.before_after: Before: any non-input click on the row called setFixing([path], !fixing). After: the same, unless window.getSelection() returns text, in which case nothing changes
contracts.visible_effect: The row keeps its ticked/unticked state (rowOff dimming at line 208, group count at lines 312-314, summary and Fix button label at lines 574-607) when the click ends a text selection
contracts.failure_mode: Synchronous DOM call; getSelection() returning null is handled by optional chaining, which falls through to the toggle. Remaining gap: a double-click selection toggles on the first click (see finding)

thread_replies.reply: Confirmed. Line 216 skips the toggle when there's a selection, so a drag-select over a name no longer flips the row. The test at reconcile.test.tsx:368-374 covers it. One small remaining case: a double-click to select a name still toggles on its first click. I've filed that as a separate consider.

structuredOutput.summary: The fix does what the reply on the earlier thread says. The row's click handler now returns early when the window has a text selection, so a drag-select over a name to copy it no longer toggles the row. Clicks on the checkbox itself are still handled on their own path. The test mocks `getSelection` and checks that the box keeps its state, so I'm closing the earlier thread as addressed. One case is still open, filed as a consider: a double-click to select a name toggles the row on its first click, because the word only gets selected on the second mousedown.
